chunks: A group narrated to me from Abul Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawood and Abu Abdullah Husayn ibn Ali ibn Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh, saying: From the mistakes of Muhammad ibn Ali in the religion in the segment of testimonials is that he narrated from the Scholar (peace be upon him) that he said: 'When your faithful brother has a right over another man, and he denies this right, and your brother does not have witnesses against him, but one person and he is a reliable witness, you turn to the witness and ask him about his testimonial. When he testifies to you, you testify along with him to the judge according to his testimony, so the right of a Muslim man is not trespassed.' The wording is from Ibn Babawayh. He said: 'This is a lie he has made and we don’t know of any such narration.' In another occasion he says, 'He has lied.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific error in the doctrine of Muhammad ibn Ali regarding single witness testimony?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi highlights a specific jurisprudential critique by Muhammad ibn Ali (likely the father of the 7th Imam) regarding the acceptance of a single reliable witness (shahid) in court, a view he deemed a fabrication not aligned with the Imams' teachings. This discussion underscores the rigorous methodology of Shia scholars in validating legal precedents and distinguishing between authentic prophetic traditions and potential errors in early juristic interpretations.
